says: In next/, every page of a ledger `read` runs `behind`, which counts `sum(rev > ?)` over every entry of the stream for the span's `lag` tag, so a reader's catch-up gets slower with every letter its inbox ever held, read or not.
proof: Experiment 295 (`experiments/295-inbox-cap.md`), node:sqlite on main at this head: a catch-up over the same 256 unread letters of 1 KiB through `Mailbox.read` took 2.5 ms p50 with 0 read letters before them, 3.3 ms with 10,000 and 13.4 ms with 100,000, five runs each.
cost: A long-lived reader's inbox only grows, so each wake costs more over the process's life, and on a Durable Object each scanned row is a row read billed; the inbox cap of ticket 1041 bounds unread letters, not this.
